findings.finding: The company's own earning-capacity table (PFPM attributable to A/B shares SEK 946m/yr as at 1 July = SEK 1.105/share/qtr, i.e. EPRA EPS around 1.0-1.05 after the c. 0.08-0.10 tax gap seen in Q1-Q2) plus Q3 seasonality puts Q3 EPRA EPS at c. 1.04-1.10 against a 1.10 bar and rental income at c. SEK 458-463m against a 465m consensus mean: in line to marginally light.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Observed report-day moves on the actual release dates (Nasdaq feed timestamps, Yahoo closes): Q1'25 -1.9/-3.2 (released 12:07), Q2'25 +3.9, Q3'25 -2.0, FY25 +5.3, Q1'26 -3.1, Q2'26 -1.3 despite PFPM/share +27% YoY; growth in line with the run-rate has been sold more often than bought.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an inference from public numbers, so mostly priced; the only unpriced element is how much of the single-analyst 1.10 rests on the earning-capacity run-rate versus a Q3 seasonal lift. If the market expected a clear beat, the stock would not have lagged into the print (-10.3% over 20 sessions); if it expected a miss, the 5-day bounce (+2.9%) and the 4/4 buy ratings would look different.
findings.independence: Yahoo consensus (same bar, not independent evidence on the outcome): https://query2.finance.yahoo.com/v10/finance/quoteSummary/INTEA-B.ST?modules=earningsTrend

findings.finding: The two Stockholm property peers that printed Q3 on 21 Oct reported positive Q3 property and derivative value changes (Wihlborgs: properties +49m, derivatives +383m in Q3; Fabege: positive changes in both) and flagged rising financing-cost uncertainty, and both traded down on the day (Wihlborgs c. -3.3%, Fabege c. -1.8% at 15:40 CET): Intea's own value change is likely positive again, and the sector reaction function into Q3 prints is to sell.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Intea has reported positive value changes on investment properties in every quarter since Q3 2024 (69, 81, 146, 143, 168, 393, 217, 155 SEKm); the NRV line has not visibly driven its report-day sign.
findings.original_quote: Wihlborgs: 'Värdeförändring fastigheter 49 ... Värdeförändring derivat 383' (Q3 property value change +49m, derivative value change +383m) and 'en ökad osäkerhet kring finansieringskostnader' (increased uncertainty about financing costs); Fabege (https://attachment.news.eu.nasdaq.com/a7c0cd3eeef2e79678edfca70bb10a90e): 'positiva värdeförändringar i både fastigheter och räntederivat' (positive value changes in both properties and interest-rate derivatives).
findings.why_not_priced: Same-day peer prints are seen by every Swedish property desk, so this is a proxy that is largely priced; the read-through to a social-infrastructure owner with 97% public tenants and 7.8-year leases is weak. If the market had priced a negative valuation surprise for Intea, its own stock would have fallen with the peers on 21 Oct; instead it was up c. 0.6% intraday.
